A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe DDAVS, and their main text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable. However, v1 includes supplementary Sections A–H, whereas v2 ends with references despite repeatedly referring to supplementary material. This limits comparison of the supplementary analyses and details.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDAVS experiments on AVSBench and VPO, component and architectural ablations, representation visualizations, and supplementary efficiency and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including additional prototype-removal experiments, qualitative component comparisons, and cross-domain representation analysis.

M1.justification: The prototype-grounded AQM, waveform-contrastive COM, delayed bidirectional AVAM, and combined training objective are retained. The explicit self-attention equations in v2 describe operations already depicted in v1 Figure 3; expanded bank and augmentation descriptions largely match v1's appendix rather than establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds ESC-50 audio to the shared-dog representation analysis in Section 4.4, extending empirical coverage to another audio domain. The AVSBench and VPO segmentation tasks remain unchanged; ESC-50 is not presented as an additional segmentation benchmark.

E2.justification: AVSBench Table 1 adds evaluated rows for COMBO, CPM, and CCFormer, while VPO Table 2 adds CPM. These are additions to the corresponding comparator sets, even though COMBO and the work underlying CCFormer were already cited in v1.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce prototype-removal conditions of 20%, 50%, 80%, and 100%, plus a cross-dataset embedding comparison. Existing benchmark metrics and stated main training settings remain unchanged. Freezing the visual backbone for the injection-position study is newly disclosed, without evidence that this existing experiment's setting changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds an AQM+AVAM control that isolates COM's contribution, qualitative component ablations, prototype-removal robustness tests, a weak-target heatmap case, and cross-domain t-SNE analysis. These substantially expand diagnostic evidence. Backbone, query-count, and injection-block studies are retained; v1's separate fusion-location and failure-case analyses cannot be matched in the supplied v2.

E5.justification: Both versions state that random seeds are fixed and report point estimates. Neither supplied PDF adds run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Under the retained reported benchmark settings, DDAVS J&F changes from 75.1 to 76.0 on MS3 and 52.6 to 52.9 on AVSS in Table 1, and from 74.80 to 75.03 on VPO-SS in Table 2, overtaking RAVS there. DiffusionAVS scores and numerous component, injection, and backbone ablation values also change. Added comparator, prototype-removal, component-control, and cross-domain results substantially extend the reported evidence; the PDFs do not explain these revisions as a method change.

T1.justification: The main attention formulas and objectives are retained, with self-attention made explicit for operations already depicted in v1. However, v1 Appendix F supplies individual loss definitions, while v2 defers these to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF. Their retention or revision cannot be checked.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that prototype-grounded disentanglement, contrastive optimization, and delayed bidirectional alignment improve challenging audio-visual segmentation and achieve leading benchmark performance. The renamed title and revised abstract wording do not materially change these contributions or their claimed scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an implicit-denoising explanation for attention ordering and interprets its new analyses as supporting unseen-sound grounding and domain-invariant representations. Its included limitations paragraph is less specific than v1 Appendix G's discussion of low light, rapid motion, mono audio, and short aligned clips; the missing supplement limits comparison of the complete later qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies bank construction from training splits, clip and category counts, five prototypes per category, and totals of 355/105 anchors. It also discloses backbone freezing for the injection study and adds a project-page link. Much augmentation detail is relocated from v1's appendix; v1's FPS and training-time disclosures are unavailable in the supplied v2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including CPM, ESC-50, LAVT, and several video-reasoning or generation works, modestly broadening contextual positioning. The central distinction from query-based disentanglement, KNN prototype selection, and existing alignment strategies remains the same.

P1.justification: The introduction and several method and experimental passages are substantially rewritten and reorganized. Bank construction, augmentation details, and backbone analysis are brought into the main narrative, experimental subsections are rearranged, and the conclusion becomes a Discussion section with limitations. The title is also changed.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 2 is redesigned from six separate comparisons into three pipelines, qualitative panels are regrouped, and the representation visualization is reorganized and extended. Table 3 incorporates parameter/FLOP columns from earlier supplementary material, alongside new figures and a robustness table.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, the AQM+AVAM control, robustness analyses, and more explicit bank construction strengthen v2. However, its referenced supplement is unavailable, limiting checks of losses, efficiency, and failure analysis. There is also a new presentation inconsistency: Figure 5(c) shows birds, while Section 4.2 describes people and guitars. These benefits, shortcomings, and missing evidence prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
